Custom Distributions

Custom PyMC distributions used by the agent models.

At present this module provides the two distributions used by the single-prediction collapsed model that PyMC does not ship out of the box: a native non-central chi-squared and a folded normal.

The reduced auxiliary R of the collapsed model satisfies

\(n R \sim \chi'^2_k(\lambda)\) with \(\lambda = n \Delta_X^2\),

i.e. a non-central chi-squared with k degrees of freedom and non-centrality \(\lambda\), rescaled by the plate size n. Cochran’s theorem rewrites that same law as \((\Delta_X + G/\sqrt{n})^2 + Z/n\) with \(G \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)\) and \(Z \sim \chi^2_{k-1}\). The collapsed model uses the native non-central chi-squared for k > 1 and an equivalent boundary-regular representation for k = 1.

distributions.FoldedNormal(name, mu, sigma, **kwargs)[source]

Absolute value of a normally distributed random variable.

A softplus transform maps the positive support to the real line. Its density retains both branches of the underlying normal distribution and therefore also supports non-zero mu.

Parameters:

  • name (str) – Name of the random variable in the model.

  • mu – Mean of the underlying normal distribution.

  • sigma – Standard deviation of the underlying normal distribution.

  • **kwargs – Forwarded to pm.CustomDist().

Returns:

The PyMC random variable.

distributions.NoncentralChiSquared(name, nu, lam, **kwargs)[source]

A non-central chi-squared random variable for use inside a PyMC model.

Thin pm.CustomDist() wrapper pairing ncx2_logp() (used by NUTS, differentiable in both value and lam) with _ncx2_random() (used by predictive sampling). Parametrized like scipy.stats.ncx2(df=nu, nc=lam). The variable is sampled on the log scale (like PyMC’s own positive distributions, e.g. ChiSquared), so NUTS never proposes values outside the support x > 0, and its initial value is the distribution mean nu + lam.

Parameters:

  • name (str) – Name of the random variable in the model.

  • nu – Degrees of freedom (may be a constant or a model quantity).

  • lam – Non-centrality parameter (may be a constant or a model quantity).

  • **kwargs – Forwarded to pm.CustomDist() (e.g. observed, shape, dims).

Returns:

The PyMC random variable.

distributions.folded_normal_logp(value, mu, sigma)[source]

Log density of the absolute value of a normal random variable.

If Z ~ Normal(mu, sigma), then U = abs(Z) has density Normal(u | mu, sigma) + Normal(-u | mu, sigma) on u >= 0.

Parameters:

  • value – Point at which to evaluate the density.

  • mu – Mean of the underlying normal distribution.

  • sigma – Standard deviation of the underlying normal distribution.

Returns:

The log probability density, -inf off the support.

distributions.ncx2_logp(value, nu, lam)[source]

Log density of a non-central chi-squared distribution.

Matches scipy.stats.ncx2(df=nu, nc=lam).logpdf to machine precision where SciPy remains finite. The density is

\(f(x) = \tfrac12 e^{-(x+\lambda)/2} (x/\lambda)^{\nu/4 - 1/2} I_{\nu/2 - 1}(\sqrt{\lambda x})\)

for \(x > 0\). The cancelling exponential terms are combined before evaluation. The exponentially scaled Bessel function ive is used for ordinary arguments. For large arguments beyond the reliable numerical range of the ordinary evaluator, a DLMF asymptotic expansion evaluates the same density to float64 precision. The Bessel order \(\nu/2 - 1\) may be a negative half-integer (e.g. nu = 1); ive handles that case directly.

Parameters:

  • value – Point at which to evaluate the density (support value > 0).

  • nu – Degrees of freedom.

  • lam – Non-centrality parameter (lam >= 0).

Returns:

The log probability density, -inf off the support.
